title: [console] List sort: filterableFields doubles as the sort whitelist, and a header click discards the view's multi-level default with no way back
body:
Two related gaps in the Console list view's sort experience, found while shipping a downstream app on `@objectstack/*@17.0.0-rc.6`. Both are capability requests, not defects — the platform behaves as currently designed.

## 1. `filterableFields` doubles as the sort-field whitelist; there is no way to open sorting without also opening filtering

**Observed**: a list view declares a two-level default `sort` (e.g. `plan_start_date` then `name`). Neither field appears in the **Sort** panel's field dropdown, and the sort rows render with blank field names. The dropdown's contents turn out to be exactly `filterableFields` minus relation-typed fields (`lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` / `owner` — consistent with the panel's own footnote about columns pointing at other records).

So the same array feeds both the Filter builder and the Sort builder. A field that should be sortable but *not* offered as a filter condition cannot be expressed: the only workaround is to add it to `filterableFields`, which also makes it appear in the filter condition builder.

**Also note the asymmetry**: a view can declare `sort` on a field the sort panel refuses to list. The declared default sort works on load, but the user cannot reproduce or modify it through the UI.

**Request**: either a dedicated `sortableFields` (spec has no such key today), or have the sort panel fall back to all non-relation fields rather than reusing `filterableFields`.

## 2. Clicking a column header replaces the entire multi-level sort, with no way back to the view's default

**Observed**: a view ships a two-level default sort. One click on any column header replaces the whole sort array with that single column. The view's declared `sort` acts only as an initial value — after that first click it is unreachable for the rest of the session; there is no "reset to default sort" affordance.

Combined with #1 this was worse: because the fields were not in `filterableFields`, the user could not even rebuild the original two-level sort by hand. Adding the fields to `filterableFields` restores the ability to rebuild it manually, but "restore the view's default" still requires a page reload.

**Request**: a way to restore the view-declared default sort (a reset control in the sort panel, or preserving the declared sort as a fallback tier under the ad-hoc header sort).

## Environment

`@objectstack/*@17.0.0-rc.6`, Console list view. Verified against a clean database with no view overlay rows (`sys_view_definition` / `sys_metadata` type=view both empty), server restarted by port before capturing — i.e. the source-declared view is what rendered.

## Downstream context

Reported from a private app repo, so screenshots are not linkable here. Happy to build a public minimal reproduction on a showcase app if that helps — just say the word.
